content: Ochsner Baptist Medical Center is a hospital located in New Orleans, Louisiana. The hospital complex is situated on Napoleon Avenue in the Uptown area of New Orleans. Originally known as Southern Baptist Hospital, it was established in 1926 by the Southern Baptist Convention. In 1969, the religious organization disassociated itself from the hospital, along with several others, and Southern Baptist Hospital became an independent non-profit entity. In the early 1980s, the hospital undertook a significant renovation and expansion project, known as Project 2000, investing over $100 million to improve the original building. In 1990, it merged with Mercy Hospital, which was located near the end of Bayou St. John on Jefferson Davis Parkway. The two hospitals operated together as Mercy-Baptist Medical Center, with the former Southern Baptist Hospital referred to as the Uptown Campus and Mercy Hospital as the Mid-City Campus. In 1996, the combined hospitals were acquired by Tenet Healthcare, and the former Baptist Hospital was renamed Memorial Medical Center. Since 1967, the hospital has served as the official healthcare provider for the New Orleans Saints football team, beginning when Dr. Ken Saer was appointed as the team’s first orthopedic surgeon. However, the hospital faced significant challenges in the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina in 2005. The area surrounding the hospital was severely flooded, leaving the facility isolated. The ground floor was submerged, and the hospital lost electricity and utilities after its emergency generators ran out of fuel. Following several days of dire conditions, the remaining patients and staff were evacuated, and the hospital was subsequently closed. It remained shuttered throughout 2005 and into 2006, with discussions taking place about whether to demolish the main hospital buildings rather than refurbish them. The hospital gained national attention when CNN reported on October 12, 2005, that the Louisiana Attorney General was investigating allegations of mercy killings of critically ill patients by medical staff at Memorial Medical Center during the post-Katrina crisis. On September 13, 2005, Tenet Healthcare Corporation issued a statement asserting that no patients had drowned or died due to a lack of food or water. However, other reports suggested that numerous bodies were removed from the building and that a female physician may have administered lethal doses of morphine to patients. On June 29, 2006, Tenet announced plans to sell Memorial Medical Center along with three other hospitals in the Greater New Orleans area by mid-2007. On July 18, 2006, the Louisiana Attorney General’s office announced the arrest of Dr. Anna Pou and two nurses in connection with patient deaths during the post-Katrina crisis. They faced potential charges of second-degree murder. However, on July 24, 2007, it was revealed that a Louisiana grand jury declined to indict Dr. Pou. On July 19, 2006, Ochsner Health System announced its acquisition of Memorial Medical Center, along with two other Tenet hospitals in the Greater New Orleans area: Meadowcrest Hospital in Gretna, Louisiana, and Kenner Regional Medical Center in Kenner, Louisiana. The sale was expected to be finalized by the end of August.
